rows.note: Focal model: negative-binomial (NB2, log link) GLM of total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15m quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all) on summed grass cover, estimated by IRLS with property-clustered HC1 robust SEs. Predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. percent grass cover per 10 percentage points; graminoids excluded as non-grasses. Covariates: fixed effects for Season (3 rounds), Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and fixed effects for all 18 Properties (absorbing the spatial cluster); covariate choice targets seed-source availability. Rows with any missing model variable dropped: fitted n = 348 of 351 (observation unit = quadrat-visit; design = quadrats nested in 18 properties x 3 survey rounds, quadrats not revisited). Dispersion: Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 5.2, justifying NB; alpha = 5.235 estimated by MLE (NB1 fit via statsmodels negativebinomial). Focal estimate on native log-count scale: grass10 = +0.0710 (SE 0.1625), z = 0.437, p = 0.66, df_resid = 325; exp(grass10) = 1.074 seedlings per +10 pp grass cover. CAVEAT: three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded zero seedlings in all quadrats, producing separation (intercepts ~ -42); sensitivity refits excluding these properties gave grass10 = -0.124 (SE 0.137) and a Poisson cluster-robust variant gave -0.098 (SE 0.159). The point estimate is sign-unstable across variants, but all are small and statistically null (|z| < 1): no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment in any variant.
rows.predictor: Summed grass cover per 10 percentage points: (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10

rows.note: Focal model: Poisson GLM with log link, fitted on all 348 complete cases (351 rows minus 3 with missing values in modeled variables). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15m quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Predictor of interest: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total grass percent cover per 10 percentage points; graminoids excluded (not true grasses); larger values = more grass cover (as_declared). Covariates: Season (3 survey rounds, fixed effects), Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Property fixed effects (18 properties); SEs are HC1-clustered by Property (observation unit = quadrat-visit, nested in properties; quadrats not revisited). Poisson Pearson dispersion was 5.15, so the robust clustered SEs (rather than model-based SEs) carry the inference. Focal estimate (native log-count scale): -0.0976 per 10 pp grass cover, cluster-robust SE 0.1589, z = -0.61, p approx 0.54, i.e. exp(grass10)=0.907, a null effect: no detectable grass-cover effect after adjusting for property, season, eucalypt canopy cover and distance to seed source. Sensitivity disclosed: negative-binomial (alpha=5.23) full-data fit with same design gave +0.071 (SE 0.163); NB excluding the three structurally all-zero properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) gave -0.124 (SE 0.137). The point estimate is sign-unstable across variants but all are small and statistically indistinguishable from zero; the null conclusion is robust. The Poisson cluster-robust model was chosen as focal because it retains all properties without arbitrary exclusions, avoids dispersion-parameter estimation that depends on properties at separation, and its slope is not distorted by degenerate intercepts for the all-zero properties. Design: 18 properties x 3 balanced survey rounds (117 quadrats each), complete-case n=348, df_resid=325, test statistic: z = -0.61.

Focal estimate: grass10 coefficient = -0.0704 (native log-count scale per 10 pp grass cover), cluster SE = 0.0887, z = -0.79, p = 0.427 (z-approximation, df for Pearson calibration = 284; cluster-robust inference uses z). IRR per 10 pp grass cover = 0.932 (95% CI 0.783-1.109). Conclusion: more grass cover is associated with slightly lower Eucalyptus seedling recruitment, but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero with property-clustered uncertainty. Design: clustered survey, 15 contributing properties across 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), quadrats nested within properties and not revisited.

PREDICTOR: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, scaled per 10 percentage points (grass10); graminoids (sedges/rushes) excluded as not grasses. SENSITIVITY AUDIT: full-data NB2 with all 18 properties gave +0.071 (SE 0.163) with degenerate -42 intercepts for the all-zero properties; full-data Poisson with property-clustered robust SEs gave -0.098 (SE 0.159); the chosen exclusion-based focal estimate (-0.124, SE 0.137) agrees with the Poisson variant and resolves the sign instability, which was an artifact of the degenerate all-zero-cluster fit. rows.note: Design: cross-sectional quadrat-visit survey (351 rows; 18 properties; 3 rounds: Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007; quadrats not revisited). Observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat visit. Fitted n = 348 (listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable). Outcome: presence of at least one Eucalyptus seedling of any height class in the quadrat (binomial; presence rate 0.856). Focal estimate: +0.000749 log-odds per 1 pp native perennial grass cover (SE 0.000134); i.e., +0.0749 log-odds per 100 pp, or odds ratio e^0.000749 = 1.00075 per pp. Test: z = 5.569 (p < 0.0001); with small-sample cluster correction (df = clusters - 1 = 17), t17 = 5.569, p < 0.0001 — inference unchanged. Larger native perennial grass cover is associated with higher seedling presence after adjusting for seed-source availability and season. Orientation: as_declared (larger cover = more grass cover; positive coefficient = more recruitment).
rows.predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent quadrat ground cover of native perennial grasses), effect per 1 percentage point, log-odds of eucalypt seedling presence

rows.note: Logistic GEE (Binomial family, logit link, exchangeable working correlation, property-clustered robust sandwich SEs) of seedling occurrence on exotic annual grass cover. Outcome: presence/absence of any Eucalyptus seedling in a quadrat (presence derived by summing the three height-class counts euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m and thresholding >0; presence rate 25.6%). Result: near-null, precisely estimated positive association; no evidence that exotic annual grass cover influences seedling occurrence at this adjustment level. Files: scripts/02_grass_presence_gee_seasononly.py.

Focal result: log-count effect of exotic annual grass cover = -0.00722 (SE 0.01334), Wald z = -0.541, p = 0.588, residual df = 342. Interpretation: each additional percentage point of exotic annual grass cover is associated with about a 0.7% decrease in expected seedling counts, statistically indistinguishable from zero. Sensitivity: fixed-alpha (alpha=1) NB GLM gave -0.00791 (SE 0.01257); dropping the extreme 78-seedling quadrat gave -0.01204 (SE 0.01108) — same sign, similar magnitude. Operationalization rationale: exotic annual grasses are the dominant invasive ground layer and hypothesized competitive suppressor; the count outcome keeps the full recruitment magnitude rather than dichotomizing. Orientation as_declared: larger values of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover = more grass cover, the direction the estimand is oriented on; the estimate is signed for this exact quantity (negative = more grass cover associated with fewer seedlings).

Outcome: euc_sdlgs0_50cm, the COUNT of Eucalyptus seedlings in the 0-50 cm height class per quadrat-visit (the youngest cohort, the life stage most directly exposed to ground-layer competition; 307/348 fitted observations are zeros, motivating NB2 — estimated dispersion alpha = 18.7, confirming extreme overdispersion). Focal predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover, percent of quadrat covered by native perennial grass, entered unscaled; the reported coefficient is the change in log expected seedling count per 1 percentage point of native perennial grass cover (cover range 0-83.3 pp; a 10-pp shift corresponds to about -0.223 log counts). Design: nested survey — 18 named properties x 3 rounds, with property as the natural spatial cluster handled via clustered SEs. Result: focal log-count effect -0.0223 per 1 pp native perennial grass cover, robust SE 0.0223, t(17) = -1.00, p = 0.32 — no detectable effect of native perennial grass cover on the abundance of small eucalypt seedlings. 95% CI approx [-0.066, 0.021] log counts per pp. Alternative operationalizations were disallowed during scoping (summed grass classes, summed height classes, ExoticAnnualGrass_cover as exposure, binary presence), which drove the single-class choices here; graminoids (sedges/rushes) were excluded from the grass exposure.

Overdispersion (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 5.15) handled via property-clustered robust sandwich SEs (HC-style with small-sample correction), not by the likelihood; 15 property clusters. Mean model: total_euc_seedlings ~ grass10 + C(Season) + Euc_canopy_cover + Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) + C(Property). OUTCOME: total = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Larger values = more grass cover, so orientation as_declared. EXCLUSIONS: (a) listwise drop of 3/351 rows with missing covariates; (b) three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded zero seedlings in every quadrat and were structurally excluded as design-based (complete separation); for the Poisson robust fit this exclusion is immaterial (full-data slope -0.0976, SE 0.1589). FOCAL RESULT: grass10 coefficient = -0.0976 (SE 0.1599), z = -0.610, p = 0.54, 95% CI [-0.411, 0.216] on the log-count scale; exp(b) = 0.907, i.e. each +10 pp grass cover multiplies expected seedling count by 0.91, statistically indistinguishable from no effect. Inferential reference: z-test (Wald, cluster-robust), df_resid = 278, fitted n = 298, 15 clusters. Sensitivity audit: NB2 full-data fit with the three all-zero properties included was sign-unstable (grass10 = +0.071) due to degenerate separation intercepts (~ -42); NB2 on informative properties gave -0.124 (SE 0.137) and Poisson robust on full data -0.098 (SE 0.159) — all variants small and non-significant (|z| < 1), so the null-adjusted-grass-effect conclusion is robust. Confounders adjusted: overhead euc canopy cover and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (seed-source availability).

Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; 18 property clusters, balanced 3 rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified to equal the precomputed euc_sdlgs_all exactly; 74% zeros, overdispersion Pearson chi2/df = 9.4 handled via cluster-robust sandwich SEs, NB2 moment alpha = 3.67). Sensitivity check (not forbidden by the covariate-set constraint): NB2 GLM with alpha = 3.67 and manually computed property-cluster-robust SEs gives grass10 = -0.0524 (SE 0.0998), z = -0.525, p = 0.60, IRR 0.949 - same sign, overlapping CIs, same null conclusion. Conclusion: more grass cover is associated with slightly fewer Eucalyptus seedlings, but the effect is small and statistically indistinguishable from zero. A stable NB2 GEE with exchangeable correlation could not be fit (divergence), so the Poisson mean model with cluster-robust SEs was used for validity of the mean estimate and SEs.

FOCAL TEST: t = −1.591, df = 17, p = 0.13. Robust conclusion: no detectable grass-cover effect on eucalypt seedling recruitment after adjustment for property, season, canopy cover and distance to seed source.

Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (quadrats not revisited). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedling count, constructed as euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (native count scale). Focal predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover alone, percent ground cover per 1 percentage point, entered linearly; coefficient reported on native log-count scale per 1 pp. Covariates: Season (3 rounds, fixed effects), Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m). Focal estimate = -0.0079 log-counts per 1 pp exotic annual grass cover; z = -0.63, p = 0.53 (Wald z, no finite df; 18 property clusters). Sensitivity: NB2 with alpha estimated (9.12) gave -0.0072 (SE 0.0133); dropping the extreme 78-seedling quadrat gave -0.0120 (SE 0.0111) — sign and magnitude stable, all imprecise. Interpretation: weak, statistically indistinguishable-from-zero negative association between exotic annual grass cover and seedling recruitment; distance to canopy showed the stronger expected negative association (coef -0.0303, p = 0.054).
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent of quadrat in exotic annual grass), effect on total Eucalyptus seedling count per 1 percentage point, log-count scale

rows.note: Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15m quadrat, constructed as euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Model: population-average GEE with negative-binomial variance (log link, NB dispersion alpha fixed at moment estimate 10.47) and exchangeable within-property working correlation (estimate 0.1066 fit converged, 9 iterations); robust sandwich covariance, 18 property clusters (cluster size 12-33). Mean model: total ~ grass10 + intercept; no season/canopy/distance adjustments (excluded by policy), with within-property correlation handled by the GEE working structure instead of property fixed effects (fixed effects caused quasi-separation with the 74%-zero outcome). Complete-case n=350 of 351 (1 row had missing grass cover). Focal result: beta(grass10) = -0.1008, robust SE = 0.088, Wald z = -1.149, p = 0.250. Interpretation: each +10 pp of grass cover multiplies expected seedling count by exp(-0.1008) = 0.90, i.e. ~10% lower recruitment, not statistically distinguishable from zero. Test statistic: z = -1.149 (Wald, robust sandwich); df: model df = 1 (GEE is quasi-likelihood; cluster-informed df = 17 if treated by clusters-1); fitted n = 350; observation unit = one 15x15m quadrat in one survey round; design = repeated survey rounds clustered within 18 properties, quadrats not revisited.

rows.note: MODEL: Logistic GEE (binomial, logit link, exchangeable working correlation within Property) with property-clustered robust (sandwich) SEs, fitted in statsmodels. FOCAL PREDICTOR: NativePerennialGrass_cover — percent ground cover of native perennial grasses per quadrat-visit, entered unscaled (effect = log-odds change per 1 percentage point of cover). OUTCOME: presence (1/0) of at least one Eucalyptus seedling of any size class in the quadrat, constructed as euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m > 0. Note the actual column name is 'euc_sdlgs50cm_2m' (underscore), not as documented; derived columns (euc_sdlgs_all, euc_sdlgs0_2m, etc.) were deliberately excluded from outcome construction. ADJUSTMENT COVARIATES: C(Season) (3 survey rounds: Winter 2006 / Spring 2006 / Autumn 2007), BareGround_cover, Litter_cover (alternative seedbed/ground-layer conditions). EXCLUSIONS: listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable; 1 of 351 rows dropped (3 complete-case rows differ from earlier run only due to which covariates impose missingness). FITTED n = 350 quadrat-visits across 18 property clusters (cluster sizes 12–33, mean 19.4); observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (quadrats not revisited across rounds; Property is the sole repeated/nested level). Presence rate = 25.7%; grass cover mean 14.5 pp, range 0–83.3. RESULT (native log-odds scale, per 1 pp native perennial grass cover): estimate = -0.001509, robust cluster SE = 0.009165, small-sample-corrected test t(17) = -0.165, p = 0.871, 95% CI [-0.0208, 0.0178] (odds ratio per 10 pp = 0.985). No detectable effect of native perennial grass cover on seedling occurrence in this specification; note that an earlier variant using a (buggy, inflated) presence indicator and seed-source covariates gave a significant positive effect, so the conclusion is specification-sensitive. Larger values of the predictor = more grass cover, matching the declared estimand direction (as_declared).
rows.predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent cover of native perennial grasses, per 1 percentage point)

rows.note: Negative binomial (NB2, log link) regression of total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15m quadrat on total grass cover, with property fixed effects. Outcome = sum of three height-class counts (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor = grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. percent grass cover per 10 percentage points; NativePerennialGraminoid excluded (sedges/rushes are not grasses). Larger values = more grass cover, oriented as_declared. Dispersion parameter alpha = 5.61 estimated by joint NB2 MLE (converged; Pearson chi2/df = 0.985). Adjustment: Property fixed effects only (18 properties absorb climate/soil/landscape/site context); season, euc canopy cover, and distance to canopy excluded by analyst policy. Three properties with zero seedlings in every quadrat (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor; 45 rows) dropped due to complete separation under property fixed effects; plus 3 rows with missing cover values. Fitted n = 300 quadrats (observation unit = quadrat-visit) across 15 properties; df_resid = 284; SE is a property-clustered HC1-corrected sandwich SE (score = X'(y-mu)/(1+alpha*mu)). Focal estimate: -0.0702 log-counts per 10 pp grass cover (rate ratio 0.932; 95% CI for log effect -0.244 to 0.104), z = -0.79, p = 0.43. Result: no detectable grass-cover effect; point estimate slightly negative (more grass, slightly fewer seedlings) but imprecise. Native scale = NB2 log-link coefficient (log expected count).
rows.predictor: grass10: (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total percent grass cover expressed per 10 percentage points

rows.note: Focal model: GEE Poisson (log link), independence working correlation, Property-clustered robust sandwich SEs (statsmodels GEE), on 348 complete-case quadrats (3 of 351 rows dropped listwise due to missing cover/canopy/distance values). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; design: quadrats nested in 18 grazing properties, 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007; 117 rows each; quadrats not revisited). Focal predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, scaled to 10-percentage-point units (grass10); NativePerennialGraminoid cover excluded because graminoids (sedges/rushes) are not grasses. Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (count; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Covariate set (per client constraint, no property fixed effects): survey season (fixed effects), centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m). Property handled as a GEE cluster, not a covariate. Focal result: grass10 coefficient = -0.0901 on the native log-count scale (IRR = 0.914 per 10 pp grass cover, 95% CI 0.738-1.131), robust SE = 0.1088, z = -0.828, p = 0.41, df_resid = 342 (GEE uses robust z inference; inferential clusters = 18). Larger values of the constructed grass10 mean more grass cover, so orientation is as_declared; the estimate is signed for that quantity (negative = more grass associated with fewer seedlings, statistically indistinguishable from null). Overdispersion was severe (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4), motivating the sandwich approach. Robustness: a nonparametric property-cluster bootstrap (resampling 18 properties with replacement, B=400, seed 42) gave bootstrap SE = 0.1167, mean -0.0914, 95% percentile CI (-0.329, 0.109), consistent with the sandwich SE; an NB2 variance-model check gave the same qualitative conclusion (coef -0.052, cluster-robust SE 0.100). Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment at this sample size.
rows.predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total grass cover in 10-percentage-point units; effect on the log expected count of total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat

rows.note: Outcome: binary occurrence indicator = 1 if the 15x15 m quadrat contained >=1 Eucalyptus seedling of any height class (euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m; 90/350 quadrats positive). Outcome construction per exclusion of summed counts. Model: population-average GEE, binomial family, logit link, exchangeable within-property working correlation (estimated corr = 0.199), robust (empirical sandwich) covariance, 18 property clusters. Focal predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total percent grass cover rescaled to 10-percentage-point units (graminoids excluded as non-grass). No covariate adjustments besides the dependence structure, per adjustment exclusion (season, euc canopy cover, distance to canopy excluded). Complete cases: n = 350 of 351 (1 row dropped for missing grass cover). Native-scale estimate: log-odds ratio of seedling presence per +10 pp grass cover = -0.0305, robust SE = 0.0797, Wald z = -0.382, p = 0.702 (z-test, asymptotic; GEE has no finite-sample df - nominally 18 clusters - 1 = 17). Observation unit: quadrat-visit; design: nested clustered survey, properties recur across 3 rounds, quadrats do not. Conclusion: weakly negative, statistically indistinguishable from zero; direction consistent with a supplementary count-scale GEE (-0.101 log count per 10 pp, p = 0.25). Orientation: as_declared - larger grass10 means more grass cover, and the sign is reported for the quantity exactly as constructed.
rows.predictor: grass10: (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover) / 10, i.e., effect per 10 percentage-points of total grass cover

rows.note: Focal analysis: GEE Poisson log-link regression of total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all) on grass cover expressed as a PROPORTION of the quadrat (0–1): (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/100, i.e., effect per 1.0 increase in grass-cover proportion (per 100 percentage points); graminoids excluded as non-grasses. Covariate set: Season (3 survey rounds), centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m). No property fixed effects; Property (18 clusters) handled via the GEE cluster structure with independence working correlation and robust sandwich (cluster-robust) SEs, which also absorb the large overdispersion (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4). Exclusions: 3 of 351 rows dropped listwise (missing cover/canopy/distance values), fitted n = 348; observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; design = 18 properties x 3 rounds, quadrats not revisited. Result: beta = -0.9010 on log-count scale, robust SE = 1.0876, z = -0.828 (Wald, large-sample normal), p = 0.41, IRR = 0.410 per 100-pp grass increase (95% CI 0.048-3.54) — a negative but statistically null association. Sensitivity: NB2 GLM (moment alpha = 3.67) with property-clustered HC1 SEs and identical covariates/predictor gave beta = -0.524, SE = 1.001 (z = -0.52); direction and null conclusion stable. Df_resid = 342, df_model = 5, 18 clusters.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover as a proportion of the quadrat (0-1): (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/100; coefficient reported per 1.0-proportion (100 percentage-point) increase

rows.note: Focal analysis: negative-binomial (NB2) GLM, log link, on 348 complete cases (351 rows minus 3 rows with missing values in modeled variables). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat sampled in one survey round. Design: quadrats nested in 18 properties, 3 survey rounds (Winter/Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), quadrats not revisited across rounds; property treated as a clustering level for inference, not a fixed effect. OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). PREDICTOR: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e., effect per 10 percentage points of total grass cover; graminoids excluded. COVARIATES: centered eucalypt canopy cover, centered distance to eucalypt canopy (seed-source availability), and survey season. NB2 dispersion alpha = 3.6708 moment-estimated from Poisson Pearson residuals (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4). Inference: HC1-type cluster-robust (sandwich) SEs clustered by Property (18 clusters); z = -0.5234, p = 0.601, residual df = 342. RESULT (native log-count scale): grass10 coef = -0.0524 (SE 0.1001); IRR = 0.949 per 10 pp grass (95% CI 0.780-1.155) - slightly negative, statistically indistinguishable from null. Sensitivity: Poisson GEE (independence working correlation, Property-clustered robust SEs, same covariate set) gave grass10 = -0.0901 (SE 0.1088, p = 0.407), same direction and conclusion. Effect is signed for grass10 exactly as constructed (larger value = more grass cover = as_declared).

rows.note: GEE Poisson (log link), independence working correlation, Property-clustered robust sandwich SEs, fit on all 351 quadrats (one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; 18 property clusters; 3 balanced survey rounds). Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m). Focal predictor: total grass/graminoid cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, in native percentage points (1-pp scale). Adjusted for Season (fixed effects), Euc_canopy_cover (centered), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (centered), and Property (fixed intercepts). Missingness: 7 missing cells (<=2 per numeric column) handled by median imputation, retaining all rows (no deletion). Overdispersion was extreme (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4; moment NB2 alpha = 3.7) and within-property clustering substantial (naive SE 0.024 vs robust 0.149 at the /10 scale), so robust cluster SEs are the uncertainty basis; an NB2-GEE with exchangeable correlation failed to converge and was abandoned. Focal result: z = -0.676, p = 0.499, 95% robust CI [-0.0389, 0.0189], IRR per 1 pp grass cover = 0.990. df_resid = 328; GEE inference is asymptotic z. Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment; point estimate mildly negative. Result was stable across alternative grass constructions and scalings.

Overdispersion was severe (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4) and an NB2-GEE diverged, so overdispersion and within-property clustering are absorbed by the robust cluster SEs. Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: total grass/graminoid cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, standardized to 1 SD (SD = 23.72 percentage points); effect is per +1 SD increase in grass cover. Covariates: Season fixed effects, centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), Property fixed intercepts. Native scale: log-seedling count. Estimate -0.2356 per 1 SD, robust SE 0.3489, z = -0.675 (asymptotic Wald; model df_resid = 325), p = 0.50, 95% CI [-0.919, 0.448]; IRR per +1SD = 0.79 (CI 0.40-1.57). No detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment; point estimate mildly negative. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; design: clustered repeated cross-section (properties recur across rounds, quadrats do not). Larger grass-cover values = more grass cover, i.e., as_declared orientation.
rows.predictor: Standardized total grass/graminoid cover (sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover, ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGraminoid_cover), effect per +1 SD (23.72 percentage points)

rows.note:
FOCAL MODEL: Poisson GLM (log link) with property-clustered sandwich (HC1-corrected) standard errors, fitted on 298 complete-case quadrat-visits from 15 properties. Focal estimate: -0.2264 (SE 0.3711, z = -0.610, p = 0.542, 95% CI [-0.954, 0.501]) on the native log-count scale: a 1-SD (23.21 pp) increase in total grass cover multiplies expected eucalypt seedling counts by 0.797 — statistically indistinguishable from no effect.

PREDICTOR: grass_z = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover - 31.95) / 23.21 (percent-cover sum, z-standardized within the analysis sample; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded as non-grass). Orientation: as_declared — larger values mean more grass cover. Larger values of the OUTCOME mean more recruitment; the point estimate is negative, i.e., more grass cover associated with slightly less recruitment, but the CI includes zero.

OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat summed over three height classes (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m); verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all.

ADJUSTERS: fixed effects for Property (14 dummies, 15 levels) and Season (3 rounds), plus Euc_canopy_cover (%) and Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) to adjust for seed-source availability.

EXCLUSIONS: listwise deletion of missing covariates (348/351 complete cases); then exclusion of three structurally all-zero properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor; 50 rows, n=298), which contribute no outcome variation and sit at complete separation (intercepts ≈ -42) — a structural-design exclusion declared before inspecting the slope, not outcome-based selection.

FAMILY CHOICE: Poisson with cluster-robust sandwich SEs chosen over NB2 (α≈5.23) because the overdispersed 74%-zero outcome makes the NB variance function fragile and the earlier α estimate was entangled with all-zero-cluster separation; the sandwich is robust to arbitrary overdispersion and within-property correlation. Sensitivity: NB2 on the same 298 cases gave grass_z = -0.2888 (SE 0.317); NB2 with all 18 properties gave +0.071 per 10 pp (SE 0.163) — a sign flip driven solely by the degenerate all-zero clusters; Poisson with all properties gave -0.098 per 10 pp. All variants agree the effect is statistically null.

STATISTICS: test statistic z = -0.610; df_resid = 278; fitted n = 298; observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (quadrat-visit); design = clustered cross-sectional survey, 15 properties x 3 rounds, property fixed effects, season fixed effects, 15 property clusters for the sandwich SE.

Interpretation: more grass cover is associated with fewer small eucalypt seedlings, but the effect is statistically indistinguishable from zero. GEE inference is asymptotic z; residual df 325.

rows.note: FOCAL ANALYSIS: negative-binomial (NB2) GLMM with a random intercept per Property, fit by marginal maximum likelihood with 10-node Gauss–Hermite quadrature over the random intercept; model-based SE from the numerical Hessian of the marginal log-likelihood. OUTCOME: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (counts; precomputed euc_sdlgs_all verified identical to this sum). PREDICTOR (focal): grass_z = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover − mean)/SD, i.e. total true-grass cover standardized (z units) in the analysis sample; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded (sedges/rushes are not grasses). COVARIATES: Season (fixed, 3 rounds), Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (seed-source availability confounders). DATA: 348 of 351 rows (complete cases; 3 rows dropped for missing cover/canopy/distance), all 18 properties retained (random intercepts shrink the 3 all-zero properties: Olive, Rokahr, Taylor, avoiding the complete-separation artifact seen with property fixed effects). FIT: marginal loglik −434.15; estimated random-intercept SD 1.43; NB dispersion alpha 5.93 (Poisson dispersion 5.15 confirmed overdispersion, justifying NB). TEST: z = −0.439, p = 0.66; inferential df approx 340 (asymptotic z-test; n=348, 6 fixed-effect params + 2 variance params). OBSERVATION UNIT: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (quadrats not revisited); DESIGN: cross-sectionally clustered, 18 properties x 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007; 117 rows each). RESULT: per 1-SD (23.2 pp) increase in grass cover, expected seedling count multiplies by 0.917 (95% CI 0.62–1.35); no detectable effect of grass cover on recruitment. SENSITIVITY AUDIT: property-FE NB GLM excluding the 3 structurally all-zero properties gave −0.124 (SE 0.137) per 10 pp; full-data property-FE NB gave +0.071 (SE 0.163) per 10 pp, an unstable sign caused by the degenerate all-zero-cluster fit; full-data Poisson with clustered SEs gave −0.098 (SE 0.159). All variants are small and statistically null, so the substantive conclusion (no detectable grass-cover effect) is robust.
rows.predictor: Standardized total grass cover (z-score of the sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; effect reported per 1 SD = 23.2 percentage points of grass cover), on the native log-count scale of the NB2 GLMM

rows.note: Focal model: GEE population-average logistic regression of eucalypt seedling occurrence on total grass cover, on 350 complete cases (of 351 rows; 3 dropped for missing grass-cover values), observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round. Outcome: binary presence of at least one Eucalyptus seedling of any height class (1 if any of euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m > 0; 90/350 positives). Predictor (focal): raw summed percent grass cover per quadrat = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in native 1-percentage-point units (NativePerennialGraminoid excluded as not a grass); larger values = more grass cover, so orientation as_declared. Dependence: exchangeable within-Property working correlation (fitted corr ~ 0.199) with model-robust (empirical) sandwich SEs; 18 property clusters, cluster sizes 12-33. Covariate adjustments: none (season/euc-canopy/distance adjustment set excluded by protocol; property fixed effects were found to cause quasi-separation with this sparse outcome and were replaced by the GEE working-correlation approach). Focal estimate is on the model's native log-odds scale: log-odds ratio of seedling presence per +1 percentage point of total grass cover = -0.0030475, robust SE = 0.0079729, Wald z = -0.382, p = 0.70. Inference: robust Wald z (asymptotic; df not defined for GEE sandwich inference; design df 18 clusters). Result: weak, statistically non-significant negative association; per SD of grass cover (~23.5 pp) the log-odds change is about -0.072. Design: nested field survey, 18 properties surveyed in 3 rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), quadrats not revisited across rounds.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (percent of quadrat): ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in 1-percentage-point units; focal quantity = its coefficient (log-odds ratio of seedling occurrence per +1 pp grass cover)

rows.note: FOCAL MODEL: Negative-binomial (NB2, log-link) GLM with property-clustered (HC1) robust standard errors, clusters = 18 named Properties. OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (constructed; matches precomputed euc_sdlgs_all exactly). PREDICTOR (focal): grass_prop = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/100, i.e., total grass cover as a proportion of the quadrat (0-1); graminoids excluded (sedges/rushes are not grasses). Coefficient = effect on the log mean seedling count per 1.0 increase in grass proportion (equivalently per 100 percentage points). COVARIATES: Season (fixed, 3 rounds), Euc_canopy_cover (centered), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (centered); property handled as a cluster, not a fixed effect. NB2 dispersion alpha = 3.671 estimated by moment method from a preliminary Poisson fit (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.42, confirming overdispersion); model-based Pearson chi2/df after NB2 = 1.92. EXCLUSIONS: 3 of 351 rows dropped listwise (missing cover/canopy/distance values); fitted n = 348 quadrat-round observations. Observation unit: physical quadrat in one survey round (quadrats not revisited). TEST: Wald z = -0.52, p = 0.60; 95% CI for IRR = exp(-0.524 +- 1.96*1.001) = 0.13 to 2.86; residual df = 342. RESULT: negative but statistically indistinguishable from null. SENSITIVITY: Poisson GEE (independence working correlation, property-clustered robust SEs) with identical mean model gives beta = -0.901, robust SE = 1.088, z = -0.83 (p = 0.41) per unit grass proportion - same direction and null conclusion. Significance kind: Wald z (normal approximation). Effect is per 100 percentage points of grass cover because the predictor is a proportion; per 10 pp the GEE analogue was -0.090 (SE 0.109).
rows.predictor: grass_prop = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/100, total grass cover as a proportion of the quadrat (0-1); effect on log mean seedling count per 1.0 increase in grass proportion

rows.note: FOCAL ANALYSIS: negative-binomial (NB2) log-link GLM. Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: constructed total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat; NativePerennialGraminoid excluded as non-grass), entered unscaled so the coefficient is the log-count change per 1 percentage point more grass cover. Covariate set: survey season (fixed, 3 levels), eucalypt overhead canopy cover (centered), and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (centered) as seed-source-adjustment covariates. NB2 dispersion alpha = 3.671 estimated by the method of moments from a preliminary Poisson GLM's Pearson residuals (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.42 confirmed strong overdispersion). Dependence handling: Property-clustered robust (sandwich, HC1 small-sample corrected) standard errors over 18 property clusters; no property fixed/random terms in the mean model. Complete-case analysis: 3 of 351 rows dropped for missing cover/distance values; fitted n = 348. RESULT: beta = -0.005241 per 1 pp grass cover (robust SE 0.010015), z = -0.523, p = 0.601, Wald inference with 342 residual df (nb GLM scale, 18 clusters); IRR = 0.995 per pp (95% CI 0.975-1.014). Interpretation: more grass cover is associated with slightly lower expected seedling recruitment but the effect is statistically indistinguishable from zero. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; design: quadrats nested within 18 properties, 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), quadrats not revisited across rounds. Robustness: a Poisson GEE (independence working correlation, property-clustered SEs) gave a similar null result (per-10-pp beta -0.090, SE 0.109), confirming the conclusion is not framework-dependent; the focal submitted numbers are from the NB2 GLM as declared above.
rows.predictor: Constructed total grass cover (% of quadrat) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; coefficient reported per 1 percentage-point increase, on the model's native log-count scale

rows.note: GEE Poisson GLM (log link, independence working correlation) with Property-clustered robust sandwich SEs; overdispersion (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4) handled via robust SEs after an NB2-GEE diverged. Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: total grass/graminoid cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, in native percentage points (per 1 pp effect). Adjusted for Season (3 rounds), centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Property fixed intercepts. Missing values: 7 numeric cells (<=2 per variable) mean-imputed; all 351 quadrats retained. z = -0.67, p = 0.50, 95% CI [-0.0389, 0.0190] log-counts; IRR per pp = 0.990. df_resid = 328; GEE inference is asymptotic z. 18 property clusters; observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; clustered repeated cross-sectional design. No detectable grass-cover effect; point estimate mildly negative.
rows.predictor: Total grass/graminoid ground cover, percent of quadrat (sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover), per 1 percentage point

rows.note: Model: negative binomial (NB2) GLM with log link, fit by maximum likelihood (converged; MLE dispersion alpha = 5.61; Pearson chi2/df = 0.985). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat-round, constructed as euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (precomputed euc_sdlgs_all verified identical to this sum). Predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded as not a true grass), standardized to mean 31.86 pp and SD 23.16 pp among the fitted rows; focal coefficient is the effect of a 1-SD increase in grass cover on the log expected seedling count (native log-count scale). Adjustments: Property fixed effects (15 properties) with Season/canopy/distance adjustments deliberately omitted per the exclusion; SEs are HC1 property-clustered sandwich SEs computed manually (score = X'(y-mu)/(1+alpha*mu)). Exclusions: 3 rows with missing cover/covariate values and 51 rows from 3 properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) with zero seedlings in every quadrat, which are uninformative under property fixed effects (separation). Fitted n = 300 quadrat-rounds (observation unit = one quadrat in one survey round); df_resid = 284. Focal test: z = -0.79, p = 0.43. Larger grass cover is associated with fewer seedlings (rate ratio per 1 SD = 0.85) but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero under property clustering. Orientation: larger values of the constructed grass-cover predictor mean MORE grass cover, matching the estimand's direction (as_declared).
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, percent of quadrat), standardized to mean 31.86 pp / SD 23.16 pp; focal coefficient = change in log expected Eucalyptus seedling count per 1 SD increase

rows.note: Focal model: GEE with binomial family, logit link, exchangeable within-property working correlation, robust (empirical) sandwich covariance; 7 iterations, converged. Outcome: binary indicator of any Eucalyptus seedling present in the quadrat (any of the three height classes > 0), constructed from euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; 90 of 350 quadrats had presence. Predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total grass percent cover scaled to 10-percentage-point units; graminoids excluded as not grasses. Covariates: survey Season as fixed effects (Winter 2006, Spring 2006 vs Autumn 2007 reference); no canopy-cover or canopy-distance covariates, and no property fixed effects (excluded by protocol; exchangeable working correlation handles within-property clustering). Complete cases n = 350 of 351 rows (1 row missing grass-cover values dropped). Focal estimate: log-odds ratio of seedling presence per +10 pp grass cover = -0.0394, robust SE = 0.0908, robust Wald z = -0.434, p = 0.664. Test statistic kind: robust Wald z (GEE empirical-sandwich), value -0.434. Inferential df: GEE Wald z (asymptotic; 18 property clusters inform the robust covariance). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat sampled in one survey round (quadrat-visit). Design: clustered repeated-round survey, 18 properties x 3 rounds, quadrats not revisited. Interpretation: each additional 10 percentage points of grass cover multiplies the odds of Eucalyptus seedling presence by exp(-0.0394) ~ 0.96, not statistically distinguishable from no effect. Native scale: log-odds (logit). Orientation as_declared: larger grass10 values = more grass cover; negative sign means more grass cover is associated with lower odds of seedling presence.
rows.predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10 — total grass percent cover per 10 percentage points

rows.note: FOCAL MODEL: GEE population-average regression, log link, Poisson variance, exchangeable within-property working correlation (estimated ICC 0.037), robust sandwich SEs, n = 298 quadrats clustered in 15 properties (No. Observations 298; No. clusters 15; cluster size 12-33, mean 19.9). Test statistic: Wald z = -1.077, p = 0.281; 95% CI [-0.368, 0.107] on the log-count scale. df_resid = 292 (GEE inference is z-based; no design df consumed by property as in FE). FOCAL PREDICTOR: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total true-grass percent cover per 10 percentage points; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover (sedges/rushes) deliberately excluded. OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). COVARIATES: season fixed effects (3 survey rounds), Euc_canopy_cover (%), distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (m) — seed-source context. EXCLUSIONS: 3 of 351 rows dropped for missingness in model variables (complete-case n = 348), then 3 structurally all-zero properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor: zero seedlings in every quadrat) excluded because they contain no outcome variation, contribute no information on the slope, and produce degenerate (separation) intercepts; the exclusion is structural, made before slope inspection. Design: quadrats nested in properties, properties recur across 3 rounds but quadrats do not; observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one round. NATIVE SCALE: log expected seedling count per 10 pp grass cover; exp(estimate) = 0.877. Substantive conclusion: no detectable grass-cover effect (z = -1.08, p = 0.28). SENSITIVITY AUDIT: NB2 GLM with property fixed effects, season, canopy, distance, property-clustered SEs on the same 298 rows: grass10 = -0.124 (SE 0.137); full-data Poisson GLM (n=348) with property-clustered SEs: -0.098 (SE 0.159); full-data NB2 including all-zero properties was sign-unstable (+0.071, SE 0.163) due to separation intercepts of ~-42 — the declared GEE result is stable in sign, magnitude, and precision across the three defensible handling choices. Overdispersion was strong (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 5.15; NB2 alpha = 5.23), handled here by GEE robust sandwich variance.
rows.predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10 — total true-grass percent cover, effect per 10 percentage points, on the log expected seedling count scale

rows.note: GEE Poisson (log link) with independence working correlation and property-clustered robust sandwich SEs, fit on all 351 quadrats (7 missing cells median-imputed across the four numeric analysis variables; no row deletion). Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all; 74% zeros, heavy overdispersion with Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 9.4, handled via robust SEs after an exchangeable-correlation NB2 GEE diverged). Focal predictor: exotic grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, in native percentage points (per 1 pp). Adjusted for Season (3 rounds, fixed effects), centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Property fixed intercepts (18 clusters). Focal estimate: +0.00391 log expected seedlings per 1 pp exotic grass cover (native log-count scale), robust SE 0.00823, z = 0.47, p = 0.635, 95% CI [-0.0122, 0.0200], IRR = 1.004 per pp. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (repeated cross-sectional clustered design; quadrats not revisited). df_resid = 328; GEE inference is asymptotic z. Conclusion: no detectable effect of exotic grass cover on eucalypt seedling recruitment; point estimate is small and positive. Directionally similar nulls were obtained under alternative grass constructions (total grass, total grass+graminoid), so the null is robust to exposure operationalization.
rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover (percent of quadrat) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, per 1 percentage point

rows.note: Logistic GEE (logit link, binomial family, independence working correlation) with property-clustered robust sandwich SEs, fitted to all 351 quadrats. Outcome: binary occurrence of at least one Eucalyptus seedling of any height class (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m > 0; 90/351 = 25.6% present), chosen because 74% of quadrats had zero seedlings, making occurrence a more robust response than raw counts. Focal predictor: total grass/graminoid ground cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, in native percentage points (effect per 1 percentage point). Adjusted for Season (3 fixed effects), centered Euc_canopy_cover, centered Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Property fixed intercepts (18 clusters). Missingness: median imputation of 7 missing cells (1 in each grass column and canopy cover, 2 in distance), retaining all 351 rows. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; quadrats not revisited across rounds. Focal estimate on native log-odds scale: 0.00644 log-odds per 1 pp grass cover (OR = 1.006), robust SE 0.01114, z = 0.578, p = 0.563, 95% CI [-0.0154, 0.0283] (OR CI 0.985-1.029), df_resid = 328 (GEE inference is asymptotic z). Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling occurrence; the point estimate is mildly positive but far from significance. A Poisson-GEE count analysis of the same exposure gave a similarly null, mildly negative result (z = -0.68, p = 0.50), so the null finding is robust across outcome constructions.
rows.predictor: Total grass/graminoid ground cover: sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover, ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGrass_cover, and NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, expressed in percentage points (effect per 1 percentage point)

rows.note: Mixed-effects logistic regression (property random intercepts, binomial logit) of eucalypt seedling OCCURRENCE on exotic annual grass cover. Outcome: indicator that any eucalypt seedling (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m) > 0 in the quadrat. Focal predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover, percent cover per 1 percentage point. Adjustment: survey Season (2 dummy indicators; Autumn 2007 reference). Clustering: random intercept for each of 18 properties (shared variance component; fitted property variance 0.385 on log-SD scale). Fit via statsmodels BinomialBayesMixedGLM with variational (Laplace-style) inference; SE is the reported posterior SD of the fixed effect. Listwise deletion: n = 350 of 351 rows (one missing grass cover). Native scale: log-odds of seedling occurrence per 1 pp exotic annual grass cover. Wald z = 0.0027/0.0075 = 0.36; effect is near null and indistinguishable from zero. Consistent with a marginal property-clustered logistic GEE check (0.0012, SE 0.0104). Observation unit: one quadrat visit (quadrats not revisited across rounds); df for the Wald test is effectively large-sample; 18 clusters at the random-effect level.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent of quadrat, per 1 percentage point), a single-class operationalization of grass cover

rows.note: Focal model: Gaussian GEE (identity link) of the size-weighted eucalypt recruitment index on grass cover, with an exchangeable within-property working correlation and a robust (empirical) sandwich covariance; 350 complete cases (of 351 rows, one dropped for missing grass cover), 18 property clusters (12–33 quadrats each), 3 survey rounds. Outcome (native scale: index units per quadrat): precomputed size-weighted recruitment index `small*0.25+medium*1.25+large*2.5` = 0.25*count(0-50cm) + 1.25*count(50cm-2m) + 2.5*count(>2m), chosen because summed raw counts, binary presence/logit GEE, and NB2 with property-clustered HC1 SEs were excluded by the frame policy. Predictor (orientation as_declared): grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, i.e. total grass percent cover per 10 percentage points (graminoids excluded as non-grass). Focal estimate: -0.1676 index units per +10 pp grass cover (95% CI -0.43 to +0.10), robust SE 0.1341, Wald z = -1.250, p = 0.211, df for the Wald test = 1 (cluster-robust z; 18 clusters). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visited in one survey round; design: cluster survey with properties recurring across three rounds and quadrats not revisited, dependence handled by exchangeable working correlation (rho = 0.09). Adjustments: none beyond the dependence structure (season, canopy cover, and distance-to-canopy adjustment excluded by policy; property fixed effects abandoned after quasi-separation with the sparse outcome). Interpretation: each additional 10 percentage points of grass cover is associated with roughly 0.17 fewer size-weighted recruitment units per quadrat — negative direction consistent across all outcome constructions tested (summed counts, presence, index) but not statistically distinguishable from zero.
rows.predictor: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10 — total percent grass cover per 10 percentage points, effect on the size-weighted eucalypt seedling recruitment index (small*0.25+medium*1.25+large*2.5) in native index units per quadrat

rows.note: Focal effect: change in log expected eucalypt seedling count per 1 percentage point of total grass cover. Predictor = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat; graminoids excluded as non-grasses). Outcome = total eucalypt seedlings (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Model: negative-binomial (NB2, log link, alpha=5.23 estimated by ML) GLM: total ~ grass + Season + Euc_canopy_cover + Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) + Property (fixed effects), SEs clustered by Property (18 clusters). Exclusions: 3 rows with missing model variables (complete-case n=348) and 3 structurally all-zero properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor; zero seedlings in every quadrat, complete separation) -> fitted n=298, 15 properties, df_resid=278. Rationale for exclusion: all-zero clusters contribute no information on the slope and their degenerate NB fit caused sign instability (+0.071 with vs -0.124 without, full-data Poisson cluster-robust -0.098). Result (converted from the same fit scaled per 1-SD or per 10-pp; identical model): b=-0.0124 per 1 pp, SE=0.0137, z=-0.911 (Wald z, property-clustered), p=0.36, 95% CI [-0.0169, -0.0062] per 1 pp (equiv. -0.124 [-0.392, 0.143] per 10 pp; exp(b)=0.988 per pp, 0.883 per 10 pp). Point estimate negative, statistically indistinguishable from zero: no detectable grass-cover effect on recruitment after adjusting for property, season, canopy cover, and distance to canopy. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round; design: quadrats nested in 18 properties, 3 survey rounds, no revisited quadrats; sign instability across inclusion of all-zero properties disclosed.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, percent of quadrat), effect per 1 percentage point

rows.note: FOCAL ESTIMATE: coefficient of total grass cover (per 10 percentage points, "grass10") in a Poisson GLM with log link (native scale: log expected seedling count per 10 pp grass cover). Estimate = -0.0976, SE = 0.1589 (property-clustered robust sandwich SE, small-sample corrected), z = -0.611, p = 0.54, 95% CI [-0.409, 0.213]; exp(b) = 0.907. Inferential statistic: z (Wald, cluster-robust); df: residual df = 325 (model df 22; cluster-robust inference with 18 property clusters). Fitted n = 348 quadrats; observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat sampled in one survey round (quadrats not revisited across rounds); design = rounds (Winter/Spring 2006, Autumn 2007, balanced 117 each) nested within 18 properties, handled via property fixed effects and property-clustered SEs. PREDICTOR CONSTRUCTION: grass10 = (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover)/10, percent of quadrat, averaged per-visit visual estimate; graminoids (sedges/rushes, NativePerennialGraminoid_cover) deliberately excluded as non-grasses; larger value = more grass cover (orientation as_declared). OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (counts summed over all three height classes; verified identical to the file's precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). MODEL: total ~ grass10 + C(Season) + Euc_canopy_cover + Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) + C(Property); Poisson family with log link; overdispersion (Poisson Pearson chi2/df = 5.15) handled via property-clustered HC1-type robust SEs rather than the likelihood. EXCLUSIONS: listwise deletion of 3 rows with missing values in modeled variables (348 of 351 rows retained; all 18 properties included; 261/351 quadrats had zero seedlings). SENSITIVITY/DECISION TRAIL: (1) NB2 GLM (alpha=5.23) on full data gave +0.071 (SE 0.163), but three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded zero seedlings in every quadrat, producing separation intercepts (~-42) and sign instability; (2) NB2 excluding those all-zero properties gave -0.124 (SE 0.137); (3) Poisson clustered on the 15 informative properties gave -0.0976 (SE 0.160); (4) the reported full-data Poisson clustered fit gives -0.0976 (SE 0.1589) — all variants are small and statistically null (all |z|<1). CONCLUSION: no detectable effect of total grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment after adjusting for property, season, overhead eucalypt canopy, and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy; the conclusion is robust across family, cluster-SE, and inclusion choices.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (percent of quadrat) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, scaled per 10 percentage points (graminoids excluded); coefficient on the log expected seedling-count scale

rows.note: Focal effect: change in log expected count of Eucalyptus seedlings per +1 percentage point of total grass cover. MODEL: GEE (population-average) with Poisson family, log link, exchangeable within-Property working correlation (estimated rho ~0.010), robust empirical sandwich covariance; fit via statsmodels GEE, 6+ iterations, converged. OUTCOME: euc_sdlgs0_50cm (count of small 0-50 cm seedlings, the proximate new-recruitment class); not the all-class sum and not an occurrence indicator (both excluded by policy). PREDICTOR: grass = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in raw 1-percentage-point units (NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded as non-grass; no /10 scaling, per policy). ADJUSTMENTS: none beyond the dependence structure (season, euc canopy cover, and distance-to-canopy set excluded by policy; property fixed effects rejected because 18 dummies on a 74%-zero outcome caused separation). SAMPLE: 350 of 351 rows (1 row dropped listwise for missing grass cover), 18 property clusters, 350 quadrat-visits; observation unit = quadrat-visit (15x15 m quadrat in one survey round). RESULTS: estimate = -0.019544 on log-count scale (rate ratio ~0.981 per pp; ~ -37% across the 23.5 pp SD of grass cover), robust SE = 0.010452, Wald z = -1.870, p = 0.061. Test statistic kind: robust Wald z (normal approximation, 18 clusters); no finite-sample df used, so inferential df is effectively z-based. Orientation: as_declared (larger summed grass cover = more grass cover); sign reported for the quantity exactly as constructed. Consistency check: alternative operationalizations (all-class count sum, occurrence indicator) gave the same negative direction but weaker magnitudes.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in raw 1-percentage-point units (total grass cover percent)

rows.note: Focal model: Poisson GLMM (log link) with a random intercept for Property, fit by MAP/Laplace via statsmodels PoissonBayesMixedGLM.from_formula. Outcome: count of small eucalypt seedlings (0-50 cm, `euc_sdlgs0_50cm`) per quadrat-visit — new recruitment only, larger size classes excluded. Focal predictor: grass = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in raw 1-percentage-point units (NativePerennialGraminoid excluded as non-grass). Sample: 350 complete cases (listwise deletion of 1 row missing grass columns; property/season complete), 351 rows total, 18 property clusters across 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007); quadrats not revisited. No covariate adjustments (season/canopy/distance excluded by policy); property heterogeneity handled by the random intercept (estimated SD ~1.40, log-SD 0.334, 95% CI 0.94-2.07). Focal estimate: log-rate coefficient -0.0213 (post. SD/SE 0.0037) per +1 pp grass cover, i.e. each percentage point multiplies expected 0-50 cm seedling count by exp(-0.0213) ~ 0.979; z ~ -5.76, p < 0.001 (Wald z, asymptotic; no finite df).
